style: Unscored medical actuality, a raw NHS emergency caught on a hidden mic in the back of a British ambulance at night. Talking and yelling only, nobody sings, no tune, no beat. The room carries the tension: racing ECG bleeps, a British hi-lo nee-naw horn, heavy rain on a metal roof, oxygen hiss, kit rattling in drawers, diesel engine straining. Crew overlap and cut each other off, breathless and ragged, half-yelled, unpolished. Woman medic, thick Liverpool Scouse; man medic, broad Newcastle Geordie; driver, Bristol West Country burr. Against them, a bored posh toff in his late twenties, drawn-out Etonian vowels, nasal and sneering, small and tinny as if heard from behind the sealed glass of a ministerial Jaguar. A single low sub-bass hum swells under the toff, the only musical sound. Ends on one long flat monitor tone, then dead air. 14 seconds.
exclude: American accent, US accent, American siren, US police wail, singing, melody, sung vocals, choir, strings, piano, drums, beat, rap, orchestral score, cinematic trailer, synth pads, upbeat, happy, comedy, music under the flatline, fade in, long intro
lyrics:
[Unscored, hidden mic in a racing British ambulance, rain on the roof, hi-lo nee-naw, ECG bleeping fast]
[Scouse woman, Liverpool medic, yelling over the horn]
Sixty over thirty! Fucking hurry up, we're gonna lose him!
[Geordie man, Newcastle medic, cutting across her, out of breath]
Sats dropping, he's peri-arrest!
[Bristolian driver, West Country, bellowing at the traffic, horn blast]
Two minutes out! Get the fuck out of the way!
[Brakes squeal, horn stops, engine idles, rain, ECG still racing]
[Geordie man, disbelief]
Why have we stopped?!
[Low sub hum swells. Plummy Old Etonian on his phone, bored and petulant, tinny behind closed car glass, another world]
I said raspberry-shaped hors d'oeuvres!
[Hum drops away. Scouse woman, quiet, almost to herself]
Fifty over twen—
[Flatline, one long flat tone]
[Dead air]
[End]
title: PL r4-no-score-fly-on-the-wall
